messages:
jamie: Quick heads up — ran a cross-pop latency sweep for llama3-small int8 on H100 vs A100 across us-east / us-west / eu-west. p50s look stable but eu-west p95 jumped ~220ms vs us-east. Chart: https://redwood.internal/bench/2625000000 :thinking_face:

mike: Looking at traces, eu-west traffic is getting routed through us-east proxy intermittently — hop count sometimes 4 -> 8 which would explain tails. sample hoptrace: eu-proxy-2 -> us-proxy-1 -> core -> h100-03

sana: Do we pin kernel selection per-region? Could be different kernel picks (cuDNN vs fast-attn) or scheduling differences on eu-west machines. Also quant cache warmup differences might exacerbate tail.

jamie: I didn't pin kernels; routing used kernel=auto and quant=int8-qt, warmup=200. Full quick config snippet I used:
```
routing:
  region: eu-west
  fallback_policy: prefer_local
  kernel_hint: auto
model:
  name: llama3-small
  quant: int8-qt
  warmup_tokens: 200
```

deploy-bot: Canary route tweak deployed at 2624999000 by lee — adjusted route weight for eu-west h100 from 0.9 -> 0.6 to relieve hot spot. /deploy/1234

lee: That route weight change was to offload an overloaded host pool. It may have caused more fallthrough to other regions, increasing hop fanout. If we confirm it's the culprit I'll revert.

anita: I pulled p95 histograms — the eu-west p95 is dominated by requests that fell back to the A100 pool in us-east (model variant a100_int8_fallback). Those traces show an extra ~120ms network + queue time. So routing fallback behavior + kv-cache cold misses looks probable.

oscar: Proposed quick experiments:
1) force-local routing (no cross-pop fallback) for eu-west for a 30m canary
2) pin kernel to fast-attn-v2 on eu-west hosts and re-run sweep

mike: Also observed kv-cache miss rate eu-west ~8% vs us-east ~1% during the sweep. Misses magnify tail due to recompute & additional token ops.

sana: If kv-cache warming is the issue, bump warmup_tokens or bump cache TTL for eu-west ephemeral instances. Also check batch sizing — smaller effective batch sizes in eu-west (lower throughput) will raise per-token latency.

jamie: Runbook I'm going to follow now:
- revert lee's route weight tweak (restore eu-west h100 weight)
- pin kernel_hint=fast-attn-v2 for eu-west pool
- bump warmup_tokens to 800 for eu-west only
- re-run the p50/p95 sweep and post updated charts

lee: Reverting route tweak in ~5m and will monitor.

deploy-bot: Deploy started /deploy/1235 (route revert + kernel pin) ... done.

jamie: After revert + kernel pin: eu-west p95 dropped ~150ms from the peak, p50 basically same. Still ~70ms higher than us-east p95 baseline. Planning a throughput/capacity bump for eu-west H100 pool to catch up on batching efficiency.

anita: Also please run a quantization-regression eval on the subset of prod prompts for the fast-attn-v2 + int8 combo — we should validate no quality regression before broader rollout.

oscar: :thumbsup: Scheduling the evals now, ETA ~2h, will post results in this thread.

mike: Added trace evidence to ticket #456 (X-Edge-Hop headers + timestamps). sample header: "X-Edge-Hop: eu-proxy-2 -> us-proxy-1". Might be useful to add a metric for cross-pop fallthrough count.

jamie: Thanks all. I'll run the extended sweep after the evals and capacity bump and upload updated latency/throughput charts here: https://redwood.internal/bench/2625000000/results. If anyone sees other suspects (kernel scheduling, CPU steal on eu hosts), ping me. :pray:
